NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, City Council Members will be participating via
  teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 894 8872 6533, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 894 8872 6533, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

  ROAD BIKE LANES FINAL CONCEPT
  Memorandum from David Wahba, Community Development & Public Works
  Director
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council keep the final conceptual
  design for Rolling Hills Road as it is and the use of retaining walls in the final design
  should be avoided as much as practical and can be accommodated by removing the
  pedestrian pathway on one side of the street, if necessary.
  Attachments: Staff Report

  C.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION  ITEM  -  RED  CURB
  PAINTING REQUESTS FOR FIRE HYDRANTS
  Memorandum from David Wahba, Community Development & Public Works
  Director
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council continue with Policy
  Option A, with the addition to contact Homeowners Associations, as follows:
  “Neighborhood Streets: To maintain the rural character of the City of Rolling Hills
  Estates, red curbs will not be painted for fire hydrants on neighborhood streets. This
  includes neighborhood streets with no curb, rolled curb or curb and gutter along the
  streets. Residents will be directed to request enforcement by the Sheriff’s
  Department. Recognized Homeowners Associations (HOA) will be contacted when
  a request is received from a resident on the HOA’s street; Business Areas: Red curbs
  for fire hydrants will be considered at the request of business/property owners on
  business area streets. City staff will determine if red curb is appropriate for the
  location.”
  Attachments: Staff Report

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  DECEMBER 8, 2020

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 7:00 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s Executive
Order N-29-20.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag salute led by COUNCIL MEMBER JUDY MITCHELL’s granddaughters, Fiona and
Sarah Haselton.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan & Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Community Development & PW Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Cynthia Morquecho

4.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 4A-K AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVE.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF NOVEMBER 2020

  APPROVE WARRANTS 63347 THROUGH 63434 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $476,440.73 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 110120 THROUGH
  110620; 63156(VOID); IN THE AMOUNT OF $453,568.66 FOR A GRAND
  TOTAL AMOUNT OF $930,009.39 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF OCTOBER 202

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

D.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF OCTOBER 2020

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

DECEMBER 8, 2020

  COMMITTEE AND REGIONAL LAW ENFORCEMENT COMMITTEE MINUTES OF
  AUGUST 13, 2020

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 10, 2020

  REVIEW AND APPROVE.

G.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 12, 2020

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

J.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF DECEMBER 1, 2020

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

K.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION - FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 PALOS VERDES DRIVE
  NORTH & HIGHRIDGE RD. RE-SURFACING PROJECT BY ALL AMERICAN
  ASPHALT, INCORPORATED

  ACCEPT THE PVDN & HIGHRIDGE RD. RESURFACING PROJECT AS
  COMPLETE; AUTHORIZE THE CITY CLERK TO FILE THE NOTICE OF
  COMPLETION FORM WITH THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY RECORDER’S
  OFFICE ON DECEMBER 9, 2020; AND IF NO CLAIMS ARE FILED WITHIN
  35 DAYS AFTER RECORDATION, DIRECT STAFF TO RELEASE THE 5%
  CONSTRUCTION RETENTION PAYMENT TO ALL AMERICAN ASPHALT,
  INC. IN THE AMOUNT OF $30,160.42.

5.  ELECTION CERTIFICATION

A.  NOVEMBER 3, 2020 GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION - CERTIFICATION OF
  ELECTION RESULTS

City Clerk Pettit provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION 2472 AS MODIFIED DECLARING THE RESULTS OF
  THE GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION HELD ON NOVEMBER 3, 2020 AND
  TAKING SUCH FURTHER ACTIONS AS PROVIDED BY LAW TO
  COMPLETE THE ELECTION PROCESS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution 2472 by title.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
DECEMBER 8, 2020
 6.  OATH OF OFFICE

The ceremonial Oath of Office was performed by City Clerk Pettit for COUNCIL MEMBERS
STEGURA, SCHMITZ, AND ZERUNYAN.

7.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  RECOGNITION OF COUNCIL MEMBER JUDY MITCHELL

MAYOR SCHMITZ thanked and recognized COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL on her extensive
career of public service, and briefly highlighted her many accomplishments.

A compilation video was played featuring well wishes and thank yous to outgoing COUNCIL
MEMBER MITCHELL from various colleagues, acquaintances, staff and family members.

MAYOR SCHMITZ introduced those present to make presentations to COUNCIL MEMBER
MITCHELL:

  Assemblymember Al Muratsuchi thanked COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL for her 35
  years of service to the community.

  On behalf of Congressman Ted Lieu, Jennifer Harbeck thanked COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL for her service to the community and presented her with a certificate of
  recognition for her decades of service.

  South Coast Air Quality Management District (AQMD) Executive Officer Wayne Nastri
  recognized COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

  California Air Resources Board (CARB) Chairwoman Mary Nichols recognized
  COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL.

  On behalf of Senator Ben Allen, Olina Wibroe-Benson recognized COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL.

  Lomita Sheriff Captain James Powers thanked and recognized COUNCIL MEMBER
  MITCHELL.

  On behalf of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District Board, Board Member
  Rick Phillips thanked COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL and presented her with a
  certificate of recognition.

  Consultant Kathleen McGowan thanked COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL for her time
  and commitment to the City.

COUNCIL MEMBERS STEGURA, HUFF, and ZERUNYAN, MAYOR PRO TEM
ZUCKERMAN and MAYOR SCHMITZ each thanked COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL for the
impact she’s had on each of them, and for her 35 years of service to the City, Community,
County and State.

COUNCIL MEMBER MITCHELL opened gifts presented to her by the City and by staff. She
expressed appreciation for all of the recognitions, thanked individual staff members, each of
her Council colleagues and past Council Members, as well as the residents and stated that it
has been an honor and pleasure to serve this City and community.

8.  CITY COUNCIL REORGANIZATION

MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN thanked MAYOR SCHMITZ for her service to the City of
Rolling Hills Estates and the greater community, and reviewed the many accomplishments
achieved during her term as Mayor during the difficult year 2020 has been.

MAYOR SCHMITZ expressed appreciation for the recognition, and expressed her appreciation
for her fellow Council Members and staff for their work and support throughout the year as well.
She then opened the gifts presented to her by the City and staff.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
DECEMBER 8, 2020
 MAYOR PRO TEM ZUCKERMAN introduced those present to make presentations to
MAYOR SCHMITZ:

  Assemblymember Al Muratsuchi thanked MAYOR SCHMITZ for service to the
  community during her year as Mayor.

  On behalf of Senator Ben Allen, Olina Wibroe-Benson recognized MAYOR SCHMITZ
  for her term as Mayor during this difficult year.

  On behalf of Congressman Ted Lieu, Jennifer Harbeck thanked MAYOR SCHMITZ for
  her service to the community particularly during her term as Mayor.

MAYOR SCHMITZ expressed her gratitude to the community of Rolling Hills Estates, her fellow
Council Members, City Staff and her family.

  MAYOR SCHMITZ nominated, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  STEVE ZUCKERMAN TO SERVE AS MAYOR.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN nominated, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  FRANK ZERUNYAN TO SERVE AS MAYOR PRO TEM.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

9.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATION

NONE.

10.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  COMPREHENSIVE ANNUAL FINANCIAL REPORT (CAFR) FOR FISCAL YEAR
  ENDED JUNE 30, 2020

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Auditor Scott Manno from the City’s auditing firm Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP
(RAMS) presented a PowerPoint presentation of the City’s CAFR.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN inquired if there were any items discussed with the subcommittee or
staff regarding this report that the Council should be aware of. Auditor Manno stated no, and
explained that there were no journal entries for this audit, and that everything was found as it
was expected to be, and complimented staff.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted the City’s current position and payments made towards the
CalPERS unfunded liability, noted the City’s taxation rate, and complimented staff and RAMS
for their work on the CAFR.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
DECEMBER 8, 2020
   RECEIVE AND FILE THE CAFR REPORT.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM - ROLLING HILLS ROAD BIKE
  LANES FINAL CONCEPT

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba summarized staff’s process in
gathering public input from the affected neighborhoods, noting that staff felt sufficient outreach
was made, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba explained that the bridle trail on
the east side of the street would stay in its current location, with a plan to create as much
separation as possible between the bike lane and the trail, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER STEGURA.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN reminded the Council that this is a preliminary review of the
project, and that it will come back to the Council for a more technical review in the near
future.

Discussion ensued regarding long term planning and regional funding for this and future
projects.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA abstained from voting on items 10B, 10C, AND 10D.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  APPROVE TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE’S RECOMMENDATION TO
  KEEP THE FINAL CONCEPTUAL DESIGN FOR ROLLING HILLS ROAD AS IT
  IS AND THE USE OF RETAINING WALLS IN THE FINAL DESIGN SHOULD
  BE AVOIDED AS MUCH AS PRACTICAL AND CAN BE ACCOMMODATED
  BY REMOVING THE PEDESTRIAN PATHWAY ON ONE SIDE OF THE
  STREET, IF NECESSARY.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

C.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM - RED CURB PAINTING
  REQUESTS FOR FIRE HYDRANTS

Community Development & Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  DIRECTION TO CONTINUE WITH POLICY OPTION A AS OUTLINED, WITH
  THE ADDITION TO CONTACT HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATIONS.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
DECEMBER 8, 2020
 D.  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE ACTION ITEM - HIDDEN VALLEY ROAD AT
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH - ADDITIONAL SIGNS FOR TRAIL CROSSING

agenda material).

Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
